newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CAPELLO TO LEAVE REAL MADRID AFTER RIFT WITH PRESIDENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CAPELLO TO LEAVE REAL MADRID AFTER RIFT WITH PRESIDENT.

text.p: Real Madrid manager Fabio Capello said in a radio interview on Tuesday that he would leave the Spanish club at the end of the season.
The announcement prompted renewed speculation that Capello, who says he has not yet signed with any other team, will return to struggling Italian champions AC Milan.

German coach Jupp Heynckes is the favourite to take over at Real. The Tenerife coach said on Friday that he would not renew his contract at the Canary Islands team, but that he wanted to stay on in Spain and play the European Champions' League.
Capello's announcement had been expected by most Spanish commentators.
"I took the decision to leave only two days ago after a dialogue with the club's managers proved impossible," he said.
"For a week I have had big doubts whether to stay with Real Madrid or not and I let the president know."

"One can't work in a squad where one day you talk to the managers and the next it's all in the papers...When people don't behave properly one can't work," Capello said in an interview with Radio Cope.
He denied recent speculation in the Italian media that he had already signed with AC Milan.
"It is a lie to say I have already signed for someone else," he told the radio station.
Real Madrid are currently top of the Spanish League, eight points clear of second-placed Barcelona.
"I am going to die to win the league for Real," added Capello.
At the same time as Capello was speaking, Real Madrid president Lorenzo Sanz was complaining about the behaviour of his manager on another radio station.
"He threatened to work badly to get his contract ended," said Sanz.

San's remarks have prompted several commentators to suggest that Capello may even be fired from Real before the end of the season. Real travel to second-placed Barcelona for a potentially decisive game on May 10.

Capello joined Real for a reported salary of 1.6 million pounds ($2.6 million) a year last summer, after leading Milan to four Italian titles in five seasons as well as victory in the European Cup in 1994.
Milan also lost two European Cup finals under Capello in 1993 and 1995 as well as two World Club cup finals in 1993 and 1994.
